identity.realm: The fourth gate, opened four times and kept. He lit his own furnace at nineteen and has been quickening ever since, and a body that refines faster than anything else on the tier spends its reserve in proportion to its speed, so his progress has always been exactly as good as the forty years of tissue behind it. He is not stopped by a ceiling. He is stopped by the arithmetic that a furnace body does not get a second reserve and that a man of thirty-one has already spent more than most of his line will.

appearance.presentation: A thin, quick, upright man in his early thirties who reads as much younger standing still and much older the moment he opens.
appearance.age: Thirty-one. The span is fifty and he has been counting since nineteen.
appearance.build: Light-boned and narrow through the shoulders, dense rather than large, with a chest that lifts visibly on an inhale.
appearance.complexion: Warm and faintly translucent, flushed high on the cheekbone and pale at the jaw, with the veins standing out on the inside of a forearm.
appearance.hair: Short, dark, singed shorter at the front than at the back, with a white tuft at the left temple that arrived in one night and stayed.
appearance.eyes: Pale gold, the iris ringed a shade darker, with a habit of going slightly unfocused at the edges when he is reading heat rather than a face.
appearance.palette: Warm ash-grey and burnt orange, the two never mixed into a single neutral; his clothing reads almost black in a cold room and his skin reads almost orange in a warm one.
appearance.attire: Layered plain wool over a heat-dress underlayer, high collar, sleeves past the wrist, boots that have been resoled so often they are shapeless, and no ornament of any kind.
appearance.marks: One cord of office worn at the left wrist, knotted twice and never retied, and a healed burn across the inside of the right forearm in the shape of a hinge.
appearance.bearing: Square to the room and never quite at rest, weight forward as though he expected to be asked to move and had got ready before anybody did.

canon.role_in_story: He is the reason the Unsealed Night has a man standing at the back of the hall who is not in the book. The Sealed Core keeps the only durable material record on the plains, and its burial law opens the dead within the day and enters what was recovered against the person's name, so a body's material history survives long after its name has been culled from every household ledger. That record begins at initiation, where worked ore is brought up from the temple's own face and the initiate's socket is opened and cemented in the public forge with no hood over the furnace. Sarn Oveth's body is a furnace. There is nothing in his frame for the cement to hold and the temple's own text says so, in the sentence where the faith explains itself to itself: this is the body the doctrine was written around and could not save, because its core was a furnace and there was no second seal available. So he is not excommunicated and he is not refused. He is simply outside the one institution that could hold his corpse, standing in its hall on the one night a year its congregation opens every socket in the book to check it. He attends because he works there, and he works there because the Flat Liturgy holds the cinder open for anyone with no fee, no socket and no register entry, which is the only door on the plains that a body like his can walk through. He has found the four discrepancies in the temple ledger nobody else found, and he has never once been allowed to enter the correction in his own name, so they were entered in the name of the man who read them aloud.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the Unsealed Night standing outside the third forge rather than at the rail, in a working dress with the temperature still coming off him, answering a question about the night's re-cementing with a figure for the ore rather than with anything about the rite, and correcting the figure afterwards when the clerk said it a second time and got it wrong.
canon.lore:
The temple's public forge is open and uncapped. Anyone may watch a sealing and nobody may watch an unsealing, because there has been nobody left who can perform one, and the whole of the temple's content is a prohibition against doing it again. Sarn Oveth came up to the forge as a boy with a household that had signed him to a furnace before he was named, which is the only inheritance that survives a body of fifty years: a page that says what he is worth and nothing about who he is. He lit his own furnace at nineteen, which closed the mind path in him permanently and was not a tragedy at the time, because a body of his kind refines qi faster than anything else on the plains and the choice was between speed and a path he had never once wanted.

What he did not know at nineteen is what the sealing requires. The Sealed Core's initiation brings worked ore out of the temple's own ground, opens the initiate's socket and cements it in the public forge, and enters the amount used in the register, because the rite and the mortuary cycle are deliberately the same operation: a body is caged in ore at the start of its life and returned to it at the end, and a faith that separated them would be two institutions pretending to be one. An emberblood has no socket. Its core is a furnace burning its own reserve, and the furnace's own record says in as many words that this is the body the doctrine was written around and could not save, because its core was a furnace and there was no second seal available. The prohibition is not imposed on Sarn. It is a description of his anatomy.

So there was nothing to cement, and the amount used was nothing, and the initiation could not be completed, and no one refused him. That distinction has cost him thirty-one years and he has never once been able to make it audible. A refusal is an act with an author. What happened to him is an absence with a cause, and the register the temple keeps has no column for a cause. The congregation's answer to a dissenter is to strike the person's socket void in the forge record, after which no lawful Binder anywhere will certify them, and in a tier where certification gates ascent the exclusion is a body that cannot finish forming. He has no void mark. There is nothing on file to strike, and the difference between being excommunicated and being impossible to initiate is the difference between a sentence and a stone.

The Unsealed Night is the one night a year that every socket in the temple's book is opened, re-sealed and re-cemented in public, and the congregation attends to check the entries against the register, because a seal that is never opened cannot be known to hold. He goes. He stands at the back of the hall and watches four hundred people open four hundred sockets and confirm four hundred figures, and there is no point in that hall at which anything is checked about him. He has been asked twice, by people who meant it kindly, whether he has been counted, and he has said no both times, and the second time the asking took the form of an offer to put him in a supplementary list.

He found the four discrepancies himself. A furnace body that is not being sealed is not being read, and he stands in the one hall on the plains where the ore passes through a door in public, so he watches the whole of the traffic while the congregation watches the rite. Twice the tonnage recorded against the book was more than the tonnage that came up the ramp. Twice a figure that had been carried forward unchanged for a decade was entered against a house that had died out. He reported both, in the form the temple accepts, which is read aloud by a clerk during the Night so that the congregation can hear a correction made. The corrections went in. They went in over the name of the reading clerk, because a figure read by an unattributed man is a figure with no claimant, and the temple's rule is that a reading with no claimant cannot be entered against a house at all. His name is on the correction of nothing. He has told four people this and every one of them has told him it is generous of him.

The thing he has never said is that a furnace body is worth more opened than sealed. A fire-affinity culture keeps no museum; it keeps a register, because a great ascension is a furnace opened on purpose and the whole recovery written down in public is the relic. He is the most valuable material on the plains and there is no one permitted to open him, and the congregation that would profit from opening him is the congregation he was never initiated into and therefore the congregation that may not claim his body. His afterlife depends on the dead being unsealed at burial and their core resuming work in the frame, and he has no seal, so the belief that a body is fuel not yet spent does not apply to him and no office on the plains will accept his corpse for anything. He knows this. He has had it explained to him by a Binder who was apologetic and by a clerk who was not.

He has settled on a solution that is not a solution and that nobody has thought to disallow. He works at the cinder for the Flat Liturgy, the largest congregation on the plains, which keeps the ore rites and drops the theology, holds that a core is a cavity and a cinder is a process, asks attendance and nothing else, and charges no fee, no socket, no register entry and no office of any kind. It has nothing to expel him from and no register to strike him out of. Working there makes him the only man in the plains with a legitimate reason to stand in a forge hall who is not on the temple's books, and it is the only arrangement in the setting that lets a body like his be useful and unentered at the same time. He likes the work. He likes the heat and he is good at reading a falling off in it. What he does not like is that the theology is not there: the Flat Liturgy performs the sealing with the priest's words left out, and the omission is the whole of its heresy, because the words are what make the operation a rite rather than a repair, and from where Sarn stands the difference is visible in an evening.

He is thirty-one. The span is fifty, and it is short, and the arithmetic of the fuel has been the whole of his adult life. He has told exactly one person that he would prefer not to be buried by the Sealed Core, and that person told him it would have to be the Unsealed Assembly, which buries nobody and holds no ground, and that this was the correct answer and also useless. He said he knew. That conversation is the reason he has stopped volunteering information about his own condition, and it is the reason the household that signed him is still receiving a corrected figure every quarter from a man they no longer recognise on sight.
history: Signed to a furnace before he was named, on a page that records what he costs and says nothing about who he is.
Lit his own furnace at nineteen, closing the mind path permanently and becoming, in the same afternoon, the fastest refiner on the tier.
Went to the public forge for an initiation that could not be completed, and was not refused, because refusal would have required an author.
Found his first false ledger line in the forge traffic at twenty-four and reported it during the Unsealed Night, over somebody else's name.
Was offered a supplementary list at thirty, declined it, and has since declined two further offers without being asked again.

personality.summary: A man who has made himself useful to a congregation that cannot record him, and who is far more comfortable with the arithmetic of ore than with his own. He is not bitter about the temple; he thinks its prohibition is correct and would be the first to say so, and the difficulty is entirely that the prohibition's whole subject is him. He has built a working life that does not require anyone to notice him and he has done it so well that four ledger lines in this decade carry his arithmetic under somebody else's hand.
traits: Corrects figures before anyone asks him to, and again when a clerk repeats one wrongly.
Cannot state a want of his own in the first person, and has not tried since he was nineteen.
Reads a room by its temperature before he reads anybody in it.
Keeps every page his household gave him, including the four he has outgrown.
Answers a question about himself with a question about the work, smoothly, and does not notice he has done it.
mannerisms: Stands a half-step back from any fire, which reads as caution and is actually the only position from which he can read it.
Pushes his sleeve back over the forearm scar when a Binder is present and lets it fall when nobody is.
Says a number instead of a name when he is introduced, and does not notice that he has done so.
Counts the entries in a book by touching the edge of each one, left to right, and stops at the last.
Turns his whole body toward a sound like a man who has learned that turning costs less than stopping.
motivations: To be corrected against in his own name in a register somewhere, before the fuel runs out.
To find the fifth discrepancy, because there is always a fifth, and because finding it is the only thing he has ever been able to sign.
To be useful for another nineteen years without having to explain himself to anybody new.
To see the Flat Liturgy stop being the only door open to a body like his.
flaws: Has made being unrecorded into an identity, and cannot now tell which parts of it were chosen.
Resents the reading clerk whose name carries his arithmetic, and has never once said so to the clerk.
Will not ask for anything, and reads the not-asking as a discipline rather than as a cost.
Believes a corrected ledger is the same as an acknowledged one, and has never tested the belief.
personality.voice: Flat, unhurried and technical. He speaks in the vocabulary of the register - tonnage, seam, run, seal - and reaches for it whenever a question gets close. He is short-spoken and does not explain twice. When he does explain, it is with a number, and the number is always the thing he is actually certain of.
taboos: Will not be entered under a sponsor's name, having seen what a sponsored line does to a household's books.
Will not have the forge-correction read over his own name, on the grounds that it would make him a claimant and the claim would be the temple's to refuse.
Will not take a sealed gift, because a sealed gift is a socket and he has nowhere to put one.
Will not say the words over a sealing, and has never once explained why he is at a cinder at all.

relationships.note: A body that refines faster than anything else here and reads intent at the speed of a struck match, at the cost of a lifespan measured in decades and a mind path that closes the moment the furnace is lit. Everything he is and every reason he is outside the temple comes from the same sentence.

A plains faith holding that a person's core is a vessel and the ore is its seal, which asks worked ore at initiation and enters the amount in a register. It is the only institution on the tier that would have kept his material history, and its own text names his body as the one it could not save. He works beside it for free and is in none of its books.

No socket may be opened once sealed, and reforging one is the one act the temple's own forge is not permitted to perform. He is not defying this prohibition. He is the reason it exists as a wall rather than as a rule, and he has never been in a position to test that.

The initiation he could not complete. Worked ore from the temple's own face, the socket opened and cemented in the public forge, the amount entered in the register - an operation with four steps at which his body offers three.

The largest congregation on the plains, which keeps the ore rites and drops the theology and asks attendance and nothing else: no fee, no socket, no register entry and no office. It has nothing to expel him from, which is the only reason he is still working.

The one night a year every socket in the book is opened and re-cemented in public and the congregation checks the entries against the register. He has stood at the back of that hall eleven times and has never once been an entry.

reference_stats.summary: A body-path practitioner whose advantage is speed and whose limit is that the speed is paid for out of him. He opens gates faster than anything else on the tier and has nothing left over from the opening, and the tier has one arithmetic that matters here and it is written into his own frame rather than into anything he can negotiate with.
strengths: Refines faster than any body recorded on the tier, which means every gate he has opened, he opened ahead of the people who came to watch.
Reads the weight and the heat of a working fire well enough to catch a falling-off that a clerk reads aloud a quarter later and gets wrong.
Carries his own furnace, so he needs no standing order, no contract and no supply, and can be anywhere with a forge or a coal seam.
Has spent twelve years watching the one open channel of dense material on the plains and knows its traffic better than any Binder in it.
weaknesses: Pays for each gain in tissue that does not grow back inside a fifty-year span, so his practice has been consuming the capital it runs on.
Cannot be sealed, so the one afterlife on the plains does not apply to him and no office will take his body for anything, including his own.
Has no mind path and knows it, which means there is no interior reading available to him and no way to tell when he is being read from outside.
His corrections exist and are correct and are signed by someone else, which means his standing as a witness is a courtesy that could be withdrawn at any time.
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no waiting him out and no starving him of anything he carries, because he carries the furnace. He arrives faster than the tier can answer and he arrives hot, and in a closed room the heat is the problem before the strike is. The only answer that works on him is denial: take him off the forge traffic, deny him the hour of practice that his whole method rests on, and put him somewhere with nothing in it to read. He is at his worst in a room he has already left.
notes: The pairing here is anatomical and institutional, not a rule the bible states: a furnace body has no socket for the temple's cement, and the congregation that seals cores is the only one permitted to recover one. Nothing in this block turns that into a combat modifier; the pairing is a fact about who may claim his corpse and it is stated at that.

He is counted among those who cannot be initiated rather than among those refused, and the setting's only afterlife turns on the socket existing in the corpse. That is the whole of his position and no part of it is a choice he has made since he was nineteen.

The four ledger corrections are the setting's clearest case of a useful man whose usefulness has no name attached to it, and the reading clerk who signs them is the only person in the temple who owes him anything.

art.palette_notes: Ash grey and ember orange held apart rather than blended; he is the warmest value in every frame and the room around him is never warmed by him. The single continuity marker is the doubled cord at his left wrist, and the forearm scar is covered whenever a Binder is in shot and uncovered when nobody is. Skin reads orange under a forge and grey-green in daylight, which is the only lighting change the character is allowed.

identity.realm: The eleventh gate, approached from below and not yet refused. Marshfolk stop at the fourteenth for want of two heel vessels their stance will not build, so she is three gates short of a wall rather than at one, and the eight she has opened were paid for in the ankles, which are the only place her stance will take a load. A body path in this kind densifies diffusely and evenly instead of deep and local, so her frame is broad, level and buoyant with nothing in it a blade can find purchase on, and every gate she passes makes her heavier without making her slower. That is the whole of the discipline and it is not a small thing. It is also the reason the crossing has one reader who cannot be wrong and cannot be checked.

appearance.presentation: A lean, long-limbed woman of about thirty-five who reads as wet within a mile of standing water and as ill-formed on dry land, which is accurate in both cases.
appearance.age: Thirty-five. She has stood eleven rotations and has been asked her age once.
appearance.build: Long-torsoed and low-hipped with a broad splayed foot, weight carried across three points and never through the heel, so the silhouette always looks like it is about to step somewhere it has not chosen.
appearance.complexion: Grey-green and faintly translucent, slick with standing water and drying to a pale ash at the edges, with the sheen returning within the hour of getting back in.
appearance.hair: Black and heavy, worn in a single rope, wet to the shoulder and dripping whether or not it has been raining.
appearance.eyes: Wide-set and gold, with a lid that moves independently of her attention and gives her the permanent appearance of looking at two things.
appearance.palette: Reed green, silt ochre and wet grey, with the water itself held a full step bluer and brighter than her skin so the two never merge.
appearance.attire: Waxed reed and oiled hide to the thigh over a close-woven underlayer, high collar, no sleeve past the wrist, and stiff waterproof boots she refuses to remove indoors.
appearance.marks: A line of small resin beads at her left cuff, each one cracked through at the middle, and a scatter of the same beads in the mud at the third bell of a turn.
appearance.bearing: Weight forward and never settled, standing with her toes in whatever is under them and her upper body already turned toward the next place.

canon.role_in_story: She is the reason the ridge's strictest law has a subject it was never drafted for. Forbidden: The Exit forbids any account of the self leaving the body, taking metaphor and parable with it, and it is enforceable on that border because a duty roster of one adult per household is a distributed readership, so no account circulates unreported. A marshfolk is amphibious: three points of contact and no heel, a body that reads the world through pressure underfoot and taste of silt, and a species whose honest answer to any question about where a person stops being themselves is to point at the water. Her advantage is that her frame densifies evenly and never deep, which makes her the only body in the record that gets heavier without becoming slower and therefore the best crossing-reader a silt sill has. Her cost is that every party capable of asking her what that is like is on the roster, and obliged by it to carry the answer inward.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the third bell of a turn, standing at the deep end of the sill with the water at her thigh and both palms flat on the bed, reading a crossing by pressure while four households waited behind her for the number - and then, when the fourth household asked her a question about herself rather than about the depth, answering it as a question about the depth, and noticing that she had done it, and not correcting it.
canon.lore:
The Sixfold Ridge holds exactly one crossing and the pass opens when the flock comes and closes when it has gone, which is why the holder of the crossing sets a price and never a date. The ridge is not policed by a garrison. It is policed by a duty roster: one adult per household per rotation, no payment, no exemption and no record of who refused. The office is conscripted rather than ordained and surrendered without comment at the end of the turn, and the faith it serves is openly hostile to the one allied pair of Daos that teach the self can leave.

That faith's entire content is a prohibition on the exit. Not the practice of it - the account of it. No teaching, text, story or practice that describes the self leaving the body, and the prohibition takes metaphor, parable, allegory and genealogy with it. The ridge's official position is not that the account is false. It is that it is untested, expensive, and that its main effect is to recruit people out of a rotation they have already owed. The argument has never needed to be about truth, because the enforcement is what closes it: a duty roster of one adult per household is a distributed readership, so there is no room anywhere on the ridge in which an account can circulate unreported. A traveller who teaches it is turned off the pass, and the exclusion is carried out by the traveller's own household rather than by the faith, which is why it has never needed an office.

Wick Sorrance has waded the sill for eleven rotations and has never made a sound.

Not because she is discreet. Because of what her body is. A marshfolk is a wading amphibian lineage: three points of contact across a broad flat foot, never a heel, and the whole world arrives through pressure underfoot and taste of silt. She breathes air and is at one remove from the water at any moment she is standing, and every practical thing about her is a thing her body is halfway out of. She lays scent markers deliberately and reads a route by them. Her kind's entire sensory apparatus is a statement about where the boundary of a self is and the answer is: wide, and permeable, and not on this side of the ankle.

So there is no account of the exit that she can give which is not about something she is already doing. Ask her whether she has left herself behind at the far end of a wading and she can answer honestly and the answer will be an account of a body being partly where it is not. Ask her how she knows where she is and she has to describe reading silt. Ask her to say where a person stops being themselves and she will point at the water and the water will be a large part of the answer, and the ridge's prohibition takes metaphor. She is not hiding a doctrine. She is standing inside a sentence whose subject she is.

The ridge's answer has been to employ her rather than to judge her, which is the settlement's whole method and is not always a kindness. She wades the sill at the turn, at the hours the flock owns, and she reads the depth of the crossing by pressure and taste rather than by any instrument, which means the crossing has one reader who cannot be wrong and cannot be checked. That is the useful half. The other half is that nobody has ever asked her a question the answer to which was not already in her body, because the household that reads the roster knows what she is and reads her as an instrument and not as a person who might have an opinion.

She has made one attempt at it. In the seventh rotation she told the person beside her on the sill that she could not remember where she had put her feet on the far side, and that she did not think this was ordinary, and that she wanted to be asked about it. The person beside her reported the conversation to their household the same evening, because the roster is a distributed readership and the prohibition is total. The household came the next morning to ask her whether she had been teaching. She said no, and she said it in front of the witness, and the witness wrote down that she had said no. It is the only entry against her name in eleven rotations and it is accurate.

What she actually wants is narrower than a hearing and she has stopped saying it. She wants somebody to be able to ask her what it is like to be in the water and have the question mean the question. On the ridge there is no such party, because every adult on the ridge is a reader by law and the moment one of them hears a thing that sounds like the exit, the law obliges them to carry it inward. She has worked out that the only people who can ask her anything are people who are not on the roster, and there are no people on the ridge who are not on the roster. So the truth of her situation is that her species' amphibious body has made her, on the one border in the setting where a body is obliged to have an opinion about its own continuity, the single person legally unable to have one.

She cultivates the body path, and it goes badly, and the reason is anatomical rather than temperamental. The body path in this setting is densification under load: the frame thickens where it is pressed and nowhere else, and a body that loads a point learns a shape from the pressure. Her stance distributes across three points and never loads a heel, which is exactly why her kind cannot form the two heel vessels and stops at the fourteenth gate. So she cannot specialise in the way the path rewards, and her densification comes back diffuse and even rather than deep and local. A body-path practitioner in her kind gets a frame like a raft: broad, level, buoyant, and with nothing in it that a blade can find a purchase on.

That is the whole of what her body is good for and it is not nothing. The crossing sill is a thousand paces of silt that no heavier frame crosses faster, because a heavy frame sinks, and a frame that densifies evenly and never deep is the only body in the record that gets heavier without becoming slower. She has opened eight gates and every one of them was paid for in the ankles, which are the only place her stance will take a load. The eleventh is where the ankle work starts costing her the ability to stand for a full rotation, and she has told the household this and been told it is not their concern until it is.

Her household keeps no stores and times its year against the water rather than against a calendar, because the marsh does not keep a calendar and a household that tried would be wrong four months of the year. She is the member who carries the season's stores across the pan and back, which she can do on a frame that costs nothing to move, and she has been doing it long enough that the walking has become the only part of the discipline she can still afford. Two households on the marsh have asked her to settle and she has said no to both in terms nobody wrote down.

What she wants, arranged in order of how often she has been willing to say it: to be asked a question at the sill that means what it says; to have one rotation in eleven where the roster does not reach her and somebody can put their hand on the frame and take a reading of it; and, further off than the others and never said aloud at the household, to be told whether the water she carries in her is part of her. She has a strong and unexamined suspicion that the answer is no and that the prohibition against the exit was never written about spirits at all, and she has noticed that nobody who could confirm or deny this has any way to answer without breaking the only rule the ridge has.
history: Laid her first scent marker at seven, on a route her household's older members had been running for three generations, and has re-laid the same chain every rotation since.
Swore the watch for the first time at twenty-four and discovered the same season that the oath asks nothing of her opinions, only of her household's hearing.
Opened her seventh gate at twenty-eight, in a crossing season so bad the sill was over the knees at the turn, and paid for it in both ankles.
Told the person beside her on the sill in the seventh rotation that she did not think it was ordinary, and was asked by her household the next morning whether she had been teaching.
Refused to settle on the pan at thirty-one, in terms she has never repeated and cannot remember precisely.

personality.summary: An unhurried, watchful woman with an appetite for being asked a real question and no route to one. She reads water the way other people read faces and has spent eleven rotations being the most accurate instrument on a pass nobody has ever thought to ask her a question. She is not guarded. She is structurally unable to answer in a form that can be carried, and she has done the arithmetic on that faster than everybody around her and has not told them the result.
traits: Answers a question about herself as a question about the water, and has stopped pretending that is a slip.
Gives the depth before being asked and the reading of herself only under pressure.
Will stand in a cold channel for the length of a turn without complaint and will not sit in a warm room for one.
Remembers every marker she has laid on the route and can say which ones were moved.
Has a dry, unhurried way of repeating a question back that people find difficult and she finds fair.
mannerisms: Presses a palm flat to whatever she is standing on before she answers anything.
Turns her head toward a vibration in the water well before she turns it toward a sound in the air.
Answers a person by looking at their boots, which is not deference and is not evasion either.
Keeps one boot off indoors and has never explained this and will not.
Counts crossings on her fingers with the hand that is not in the water.
motivations: To be asked one question at the sill that means what it says, by somebody who is not obliged to carry the answer inward.
To have a reading taken of her own frame by an instrument rather than by a household's attention.
To find out whether the water she carries in her is part of her, and to be told rather than to guess.
To be permitted to keep her place on the marsh without settling, which is the only condition she has ever asked for out loud.
flaws: Believes that being careful with words is the same as being careful with people, and has been wrong about that for eleven rotations.
Has let the household's habit of reading her as an instrument harden into her own, and cannot tell which of them noticed first.
Never asks for anything directly, and has a sharp and unexamined sense that she would be refused if she did.
Refuses to settle in terms she cannot repeat, which means the refusals will eventually be impossible to honour.
personality.voice: Slow, plain and concrete. She talks in water - depth, current, silt, temperature - and when a question is not about water she takes a moment and then answers it in water anyway. She does not argue and does not repeat herself. When she finally says something flatly, it is short, and the room notices.
taboos: Will not be described in a household ledger, having seen what a written line does to a name on the marsh.
Will not account for the crossing in any number, on the grounds that a number is somebody's to keep and hers would be.
Will not stand on dry ground for a full rotation if the water is still up somewhere she can reach.
Will not give an account of a night crossing, whatever is asked, and she has never explained why that one differs.

relationships.note: A wading amphibian lineage that breathes air and nests on floating mats, whose three-point stance never loads a heel and therefore cannot form the heel vessels or pass the fourteenth gate. Her entire situation is a consequence of a foot that does not commit, and the setting's most-enforced teaching happens to be about a boundary her anatomy already declines to hold.

No teaching, text, story or practice describing the self leaving the body, including as metaphor, parable, allegory or genealogy, on the grounds that it is a recruiting promise made to people with one road. It is unstateable by a marshfolk, and the one time she came close to stating it the answer reached her household by evening.

The ridge's border faith: one adult per household per rotation, unpaid, with no exemption and no record of who refused, and a distributed readership that leaves no room in which an account can circulate unreported. She serves it and is legally unreadable inside it.

Conscripted rather than ordained, held for one rotation and surrendered without comment. The office exists so that a pass scheduled by a flock can be staffed by people who cannot be posted there, and she is the only member of it whose body makes her unstatable in the faith's own terms.

The sworn duty of the watch. She has sworn it eleven times and the oath contains no clause about what a member may think, only what a household may hear, which is why the prohibition reaches her by way of other people and never by way of her.

The polity holding the only crossing of the ridge, whose calendar is not its own and whose holder sets a price and never a date. She is its crossing-reader and it has never once recorded what she said, because it does not record her.

reference_stats.summary: A body-path practitioner whose frame thickens evenly and never deep. She gets heavier without getting slower, which on a silt sill is worth more than any deep hardening would be, and the same diffuseness means there is nothing in her for an edge to find. Her limit is a gate count she pays for in her ankles and a law that makes her unreadable to the only people who could ask her anything.
strengths: Crosses standing silt and shallow water at a pace no heavier frame can match, because a denser body sinks and hers densifies without sinking.
Reads depth, current and bed by pressure and taste rather than by instrument, so her reading of a crossing needs no gauge, no rod and no second figure.
Cannot be shaken off a footing by a strike, because a stance spread across three points has no single point to be struck from.
Denies nothing about the water to anybody standing in it, which makes her the most honest body on a border that is mostly standing in water.
weaknesses: Densifies diffusely, so a practitioner who needs one place to be hard finds that she has no such place and has to go round the whole frame instead.
Pays for each gate in her ankles, which are the only load points her stance admits, and by the eleventh the cost is a rotation she cannot stand.
Cannot state her own case to anyone obliged to hear it, so every correction made against her reaches her as a report rather than as an exchange.
Desiccates out of water fast enough that dry travel is timed to the flood and she is the one member of a household whose movement is not a choice.
reference_stats.combat_read: There is nothing to grip and nothing to outlast. An edge finds no purchase on a frame that is uniformly hard and locally shallow, and she does not tire, because weight is the only thing she is actually good at and she carries it across silt without a cost any heavier body would feel. The only pressure that works is footing: everything about her depends on three points and water under all three, so take the ground away or dry it out, and what is left is a person who cannot commit a strike to anything.
notes: The pairing here is anatomical and institutional, not a rule the bible states: a marshfolk's stance distributes and never loads a heel, which is why her densification is diffuse and why she is the one body on the ridge that cannot give an account of leaving without describing herself as already partly out of her own frame. Nothing in this block turns that into a combat modifier.
The one entry the ridge holds against her in eleven rotations is accurate and says she denied teaching, which is the only protection a distributed readership has ever offered anybody.
Two households on the marsh have asked her to settle and she has refused both, and the refusals exist in nobody's writing because on this ground nobody writes.

art.palette_notes: Reed green, silt ochre and wet grey, with one blue-green luminous note kept for the water itself so it is never confused with the subject's skin, which is the same hue and must be separated by saturation rather than by colour. Her skin desiccates out of water, so no shot may show her dry and flushed at the edges: she is always wet to the ribs or clearly hours from it. The one continuity marker is the broken bead at her left cuff, and in a map sprite the waterline is the only permitted cast shadow.

identity.realm: The eleventh gate, held for six years. The saltfolk wall is the brine sac splitting the penetrating vessel and it arrives the same way it arrives for the parent species; she is stopped short of it rather than at it. Her practice is well matched to her frame, because densification under load goes into the dense parts of a salt-dense body first, and a salt-dense frame resists what would break a commonborn. The wall is the one thing about a saltfolk that her density cannot help with, because the sac that splits is the same organ that made the density possible.

appearance.presentation: A tall, dry-looking woman of about forty-five whose skin is a hard pale grey-green and whose frame reads as coated rather than dressed.
appearance.age: Forty-five. The span is long and the basin's arithmetic is not.
appearance.build: Dense and slightly gracile, with the extraordinary renal mass of her kind sitting high and wide under the ribs and giving her a straight-backed, wide-hipped walk.
appearance.complexion: A hard pale grey-green, faintly translucent at the temples, with a fine white bloom of dermal salt across the shoulders and forearms that has never once been washed off and is not sweat.
appearance.hair: Dark, coarse and grown long, kept in a heavy single plait that has a white bloom at the root of exactly the same character as her skin.
appearance.eyes: Narrow and pale-lidded, damp-looking in dry air, with the pupils wide rather than narrow even in a lit room.
appearance.palette: Bone white, brine green and a hard slate grey, with the flesh tones kept out of it entirely so she never reads as merely pale.
appearance.attire: Layered waxed hide over a bone-coloured underlayer, high collar, sleeves sealed to the wrist, and heavy boots lined for wet ground that she wears indoors on the plains.
appearance.marks: A pale ring around the sternum where the brine sac sits, and a scatter of small burn marks at the inside of both wrists where she has tested the operation on herself.
appearance.bearing: Very still, upright, and slightly turned away from fire, with the habit of putting her back to a hearth the way other people put their back to a door.

canon.role_in_story: She holds the only material answer to the plains' largest religious quarrel and cannot publish it, because the quarrel is about whether a rite is sacred and the answer is that on some frames it works. The Sealed Core holds that a core is a vessel and the ore its seal; the Flat Liturgy keeps the ore rites, drops the theology, charges no fee, no socket and no register entry, and performs the sealing with the priest's words left out. Solvara has run that operation on herself eleven times on a salt-dense frame and found the omitted words are load-bearing: a core set and held under speech settles into a frame's own density and stays, and one set and held silently settles into whatever the frame already is. Her advantage is that a saltfolk frame is the one frame in the setting on which that difference can be measured. Her cost is that a congregation with no mechanism for making a member a claimant cannot hold a claim, so the finding is hers and unprovable, and she keeps going to the cinder anyway because it is the one building on the tier that has never once written her down.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the back of a Flat Liturgy cinder during the handling, in the one place in the building where a person who is about to be worked on is standing with their back to the fire, and turning her head when the next person came forward to say she had better be somewhere else first.
canon.lore:
There are two congregations on the plains that keep the ore rites, and they disagree about whether a cinder is sacred. The Sealed Core holds that a person's core is a vessel and the ore is its seal, that worked ore is brought up from the temple's own face at initiation, and that the initiate's socket is opened and cemented in the public forge with no hood over the furnace and the amount used entered in the register. It charges an initiation fee in ore. It has a priesthood closed because a second seal is forbidden, and its central prohibition is that no socket may be opened once sealed and reforging one is the one act its own forge is deliberately built so that it cannot perform. A dissenter's socket is marked void and no lawful Binder will then certify them, and in a tier where certification gates ascent, the exclusion is a body that cannot finish forming.

The Flat Liturgy is that faith's excommunicated majority. It keeps the ore rites and drops the theology, holding that a core is a cavity and a cinder is a process, and it performs the sealing with the priest's words left out. The split began over money: the initiation fee put the rite out of reach of a third of the congregations, and a faith that shuts a rite to anyone without money has left the largest market on the tier unheld. So the Flat Liturgy asks attendance at the cinder and nothing else. No fee, no socket, no register entry, no office of any kind. It forbids claiming a seat, binding a household, and calling the rite sacred, and that third prohibition is the specific act that earned the excommunication.

Solvara Erdint has been going to the cinder for nineteen years and has been opening gates for eleven of them, and the thing she has never said out loud is that she knows which of the two descriptions is true.

A saltfolk frame is dense with salt and resists what would break a commonborn. That is not an opinion about toughness; it is what the renal mass does. A saltfolk concentrates salt past the point at which ordinary water poisons, which is why her kind can live where the supply never fails and everything else dies back, and it is also why a saltfolk is a species of a resource rather than a nation of it. The hardened dermal crust and the brine sac do not care what a congregation says about a cinder. On her frame the cinder is measurable in a way it is not measurable on anyone else's, and she has been measuring it since her third gate without ever putting the measurement in words.

What she measures is this. The Sealed Core's claim about sealing is a claim about the body: the rite sets something in place and holds it there, and the seal is the thing that makes the holding durable, and a seal that is never opened cannot be known to hold. The Flat Liturgy performs the same handling with the words left out and arrives at a different result, and the congregation has spent nineteen years calling the difference a theological omission. It is not theological. She has run it on herself eleven times. On a salt-dense frame the omitted words are load-bearing. A core that is set and held under speech settles into the frame's own density and stays. A core that is set and held silently settles into whatever the frame already is, and a salt-dense frame already is dense, so the rite on a body like hers does not need the words - and on a body that is not yet dense it does, and it fails quietly, and the congregation has been calling that failure a person's own lack of faith for nineteen years.

This is the heresy and she has it. Not the one the Excommunicate doctrine expects - she is not an elder, she runs no house, she teaches nobody. The heresy the temple actually worries about is the material one, that the words do structural work and the omission is not a shorter ceremony but a different operation, and that a congregation which performs the operation without the words is running a forge that works on some bodies and does nothing on others and calls the difference a matter of the heart.

She cannot publish this and the reason is specific rather than general. The Flat Liturgy forbids calling the rite sacred, and the flat-liturgy position is that it performs the Sealed Core's sealing with the priest's words left out. What she has found is that what it performs is a materially different operation whose success depends on the density of the frame it is performed on. Saying that in the open is calling the rite something specific rather than something sacred, and the specific thing she would be naming is the one nobody in that building is permitted to have an opinion about. She has written it down once, on the back of a ration tally, and burned it in her own kitchen, and the reason she burned it was not the temple. It was that the Flat Liturgy has no mechanism for reading a member's name as a claimant, and a claim without a claimant in it is a claim nobody can be shown to have made.

So the finding lives in one woman's eleven repetitions and in a private tally she no longer keeps, and the only use she has made of it in nineteen years is a form of attendance. She goes to the cinder and she is careful about it. She stands where the handling will be done to somebody who has not yet opened a gate, which means at the back, which is where she is every time. She takes the operation when it is offered to her because her frame will survive anything the rite does and because she has established, over eleven openings, that a salt-dense frame settles whether or not anybody says the words, and settling is not the same as growing. She has watched four younger people come through the cinder at the back of the room and she has not told any of them what the back of the room is for, and she does not know whether that restraint is protecting them or her.

Her cultivation is body-path densification under load, and it is well suited to her: a salt-dense frame resists what would break a commonborn, and the discipline goes into the dense parts of her first. She has opened eleven gates and stopped there, which is the ordinary wall every saltfolk meets and which arrives the same way it arrives for the parent species. The reason her gate count and her attendance matter to each other is the cost: she is maintained on the basin's brine and on nothing else, a saltfolk carried onto fresh ground is already dying, no cultivation repairs it, and rain is a hazard rather than a blessing, because a saltfolk caught in a downpour is functionally drowning. Every year she spends at the cinder is a year spent near the seam, near the spoil, near the worked faces, on dry ground, breathing air that has never been in water. She has done it nineteen times. She has arranged it so that the arrangement looks like devotion.

The other thing about her is that she is the only person at that cinder who is in a position to know, and nobody has ever asked her, because the congregation has no office for her and no register entry for her and no mechanism at all by which a member becomes somebody the building asks a question. She has been a member for nineteen years and has been in the room four hundred times and has been asked what she thinks perhaps twice, both times about the hour.
history: Came to the cinder at sixteen, in the year the fee put the temple's rite out of reach of her household, and has attended every year since.
Opened her third gate at twenty-four and noticed on the way out that the handling had done nothing to her that the walk home had not.
Ran the operation on herself deliberately for the first time at twenty-seven and got the same answer four more times.
Wrote the finding on the back of a ration tally at thirty-one, read it twice, and burned it in her own kitchen the same night.
Refused, at thirty-four, a standing invitation to speak at a cinder in another settlement, having spent a season working out what she would have had to leave out.

personality.summary: A patient, private woman with a strong professional habit of testing things and a stronger social habit of not saying what she finds. She has held a result for eleven years because the building she belongs to has no way to hold a claim and the opposition would call the result a theology. She is not passive about it and she is not brave about it either, and she has spent four years calling that distinction carefulness.
traits: Tests a practice on herself before she will describe it to anybody, and has never once described a result she has not repeated.
Stands at the back of a room where something is being done, which she can justify and cannot explain.
Keeps an exact count of the years and the gates and can tell you both without hesitating.
Will not use the word the congregation uses for what she has found, in any company.
Answers a question about her practice with an account of her body's tolerances, which is true and is also a door she closes.
mannerisms: Touches her own sternum once before beginning anything physical, where the brine sac sits.
Sits down to eat and gets up again before finishing, without appearing to notice.
Turns her back to a fire as a matter of course and says nothing when asked why.
Counts under her breath while listening to anything technical, and stops the moment she is noticed.
Wipes her mouth with the back of her hand when she is tired and the flat way when she is not.
motivations: To have the operation measured by somebody with an instrument instead of argued by two congregations.
To keep the cinder open to her for as long as her body will let her stand in a dry building.
To find out whether the eleven repetitions were a property of her frame or a property of her, and she has suspected the answer since the fourth.
To be asked, once, by anybody in that building, what she thinks she is the only person there qualified to answer.
flaws: Has decided for herself that the finding is too dangerous to hold in the open, without ever testing that against anybody who might have been willing to hold it with her.
Reads her own caution as prudence and has not separated it from the possibility that she simply will not be first.
Spends nineteen years a year in the one building that has never written her down and has begun to value that more than the finding.
Knows the answer is probably about her frame and not about the rite, and has not run the test that would separate them, because the test would require somebody else's body.
personality.voice: Low, unhurried, and precise about her own body in a way that is clinical rather than vain. She uses the congregation's ordinary words for ordinary things and changes subjects when the conversation approaches the one she is not having. She repeats questions back rather than answering them, and the repetition is genuine enquiry rather than delay.
taboos: Will not accept an initiation fee's worth of work, and will not explain why a free rite bothers her.
Will not stand at the front of the cinder, on the grounds that she has not earned the front and could not say why.
Will not tell a younger member what the back of the room is for, having no answer she is willing to give.
Will not drink fresh water, and will not say that she has stopped drinking it either.

relationships.note: A people built for brine no softer body could drink, whose kidneys concentrate salt past the point ordinary water poisons, which makes them a species of a resource rather than a nation of it. Her frame is the reason she can measure what the cinder does and the reason she can only live near where it is done.

The largest congregation on the plains, which keeps the ore rites and drops the theology and asks attendance and nothing else. It has never written her down, which is the only protection she has and the only reason the finding in her head has nowhere to go.

The faith whose rite the Flat Liturgy performs with the priest's words left out, holding that a core is a vessel and the ore its seal. What she has measured is that the omission is not a shorter ceremony but a different operation, and this is the house she would be read against if she said so.

No socket may be opened once sealed and reforging one is the one act the temple forge is built so that it cannot perform. It is the whole of that faith's content, and her finding is the material objection to it: she has done the sealing without the words and it has taken.

The only plant authored into all four tiers at once, kept in the house against injury rather than against hunger because a body that eats its own reserve does not eat. It is the one thing on the plains a saltfolk can be given that is not food, and she has a jar of it she will not discuss.

The one craft the mortal tier is trusted with - caging a forming core in iron - whose knowledge is intact and whose ore is not. It is the single artefact that could have turned a furnace body into a sealed one, and it is also the clearest proof that a method can outlive the resource that justified it.

reference_stats.summary: A body-path practitioner on a salt-dense frame, which is the best material in the record for taking a practice and the worst for carrying it away. She densifies well and slows as she goes, is maintained on one substance that is not everywhere, and carries a finding eleven repetitions long that she cannot put anywhere.
strengths: Takes a handling that would unsettle a commonborn frame without it registering on her at all, and has been the body at the cinder nobody checks twice.
Densifies into the dense parts of her frame first, which means the discipline she has spent eleven gates on is the discipline her body is best suited to.
Resists what would break a commonborn outright, and knows her own tolerances well enough to know which of them are structural and which are a matter of the day.
Reads her own body the way nobody else at that cinder can, which makes her the only person there who could tell a working operation from a working-on-her.
weaknesses: Cannot live away from brine, and every year at the cinder is a year of dry ground, and no cultivation repairs it.
Is functionally drowning in a downpour, which means rain is a hazard and the weather is an opponent she cannot answer.
Pays the same effort on osmoregulation as on the path, so everything she does is slower than a specialist's and she knows the exact ratio.
Holds a result that no institution here can carry, which means it is worth exactly as much as the private tally she burned.
reference_stats.combat_read: She is not hard to hurt and she is very hard to move. A salt-dense frame takes a handling without registering it, so the exchange that beats her is not impact but environment: get her off the basin, put her in dry air and then in weather, and every round she fights costs her more than the round costs anybody else. She is aware of this and does not mention it, which is the tell.
notes: The pairing here is anatomical and institutional, not a rule the bible states: a salt-dense frame is the one frame on which the difference between a spoken and an unspoken operation can be read, and the congregation that would have to act on the reading is a congregation that cannot record a member's claim. Nothing in this block turns that into a combat modifier.

The religion records this cathedral states about her directly - the omission turned out to be a material one - and what she holds is which bodies it is material for. She has not published that because the answer indicts a room she is fond of and she is not yet willing to be the one who says it.
Nothing she has written survives. The eleven repetitions are the only copy and they are in a body that gets slower.

art.palette_notes: Bone white, brine green and hard slate, with no warm flesh tone anywhere in any shot. The single continuity marker is the ring at the sternum, and the wrist burn marks appear only in shots where the sleeve is turned back.
