identity.realm: The seventeenth gate, opened in summer and lost every winter thereafter. The seventeenth is the first gate requiring both flank vessels pressurised at once, and his body holds one warm gradient for a few weeks and then not again for a year. Above the seventeenth he is excellent and seasonally addressed: a frame that densifies under load and then holds that density across eleven months of no feeding is the most durable in the record, and the body path asks for one thing only - sustained effort without variation - which is the single discipline his physiology is built to perform. His wall is arithmetic and he is not walking toward it.

appearance.presentation: A heavy-shouldered man of about fifty who reads as unhurried at rest and enormous in motion, and whose bulk is seasonal in a way nobody in the room can see.
appearance.age: Fifty-one. His span is long and his peak is not.
appearance.build: Broad, low and deep-chested, with a heavy subcutaneous layer across the whole frame and reduced limb length, so that the silhouette is a low wide mass rather than a tall one.
appearance.complexion: Pale and waxy, with a faint blue cast at the lips and nails that is deeper in winter and shallower in summer, and a slow flush that arrives late and leaves late.
appearance.hair: Coarse and dark, grown long and kept back from the face, with the roots carrying the same pale bloom his skin does through the cold months.
appearance.eyes: Small and very dark and slow to focus, with heavy lids that close entirely when he is listening, which in his species is attention and is read elsewhere as sleep.
appearance.palette: Frost grey, peat brown and a deep cold blue held low and saturated, with the flesh kept out of the warm end entirely so he never reads as merely pale-skinned.
appearance.attire: Layered heavy wool and treated hide to the thigh, high collar, sleeves to the wrist, and soft-soled boots that make almost no sound on worked stone.
appearance.marks: A pale crescent on the chest where the flank vessels pair, and a ring of small burn marks along both forearms from the frame-warming practice his kind uses and he has given up.
appearance.bearing: Immovable and unhurried, with the settled weight of somebody who is not going anywhere and knows it, and a stillness that reads to strangers as a man asleep on his feet.

canon.role_in_story: He is the only body in the setting that the Hour of the Floor does not disadvantage, and the only person seated three times with no register in which the second and third can be told apart. A longwinter holds a posture for eleven months and packs a winter as fat rather than as qi, and the Last Measure's rite is one act of attention held against the floor of the third layer until it ends, under an oath that forbids the clerk from answering, signalling, or accepting relief even if they asked for it beforehand. His advantage is that he can hold still and go without fuel while a clock running ten to a hundred times a mortal's passes. His cost is that the same property which qualifies him is the property that would hide a failure: the faith enforces the rule against a second seating by keeping no record of who was seated, and a longwinter betrays no change of state, so the absence of a register is not merely administrative in his case. He cultivates the body path and is excellent at it and seasonally addressed, and he wants a fourth hour, and he has decided not to want the register that would make it checkable.
canon.first_appearance: First seen still and upright on the floor of the third layer at an hour into a sitting nobody had scheduled, with his eyes open and both hands loose at his sides, and then still there four hours later, and then still there when the person who had come to relieve him was told by the oath that there was no relief and had to stand and watch it happen.
canon.lore:
The Last Measure holds that a law can be held apart from its effect and read, and that the reading is the only sacred act. It is the faith of the highest tier, where fifteen seats spread over three layers leave nine of the imprints surplus, so the third layer is the only composition in the setting with real slack and therefore the only place a law can be isolated far enough to look at. Everything it does follows from that. It demands one observation held by one body with no assistance and no second attempt. It forbids predicting a result, repeating an observation on a schedule, and recruiting, because a faith that could be taught at scale would be run at scale and a tier that can staff its own practice stops being able to hold itself.

The rite is the Hour of the Floor. One clerk, one act of attention, held against the floor of the third layer until it ends. Duration unknown in advance and never announced. No second participant, no instrument, no preparation and no recording while it is held. It produces a reading and nothing else: it is not interpreted, not published, and the clerk may speak of it for the rest of their life only to say that they completed it.

The clerk swears the No-Answer Oath first. During the hour they will not answer a question, will not signal, will not nod, and will not accept relief - including relief they asked for themselves before the hour began. The only part with teeth is that a clerk who breaks may not hold again, and on a clock running ten to a hundred times a mortal's that phrase means what it says without anybody needing to define a penalty. The faith's argument is that the silence is load-bearing: any report made during the holding is a value nobody seated, and a guess about a dial is a law the court never voted on.

Then the clerk is dissolved. One per observation, no title, no seat, no standing afterwards, and the faith's claim is that this is the only credential in the setting that cannot be inherited or seized. A clerk is also forbidden by rule ever to be appointed twice by the same person, and that prohibition is enforced by there being no mechanism at all to record who was seated, which the faith considers stricter than any register.

Torr Halvard has been seated three times.

Not by appointment. The faith cannot appoint: there is no bench to be left vacant and no incumbent to be replaced, and the rule against a second seating by the same person is enforced by nobody keeping the list, so it is enforced by the thing that would catch it, which is that a clerk who completes an observation may never begin another. He completed his. So the third seating was arranged by people who do not know whether the first two were the same person, which is exactly the shape of the faith's own enforcement and he has never corrected it and has twice declined to.

He is a longwinter. That is the entire reason he is the body in this record and it is worth being exact about, because the obvious reason is the wrong one. He was not chosen because he is cold. He was chosen because he can hold a posture for eleven months without changing it, because he packs a winter as body fat rather than as qi and therefore has fuel to spare in the eleven months when nothing else on the tier has any, and because his metabolic rate is slow enough that an hour which runs ten to a hundred times a mortal's is not to him what it would be to a body that burns quickly. He is the only practitioner in the setting whose body is not operating at a disadvantage during a long hold.

The difficulty is that his body is also the reason nobody can check on him. A longwinter is slow and nearly helpless during torpor, a hibernating one is a large warm immobile target, and cannot be woken quickly. The Hour of the Floor asks for exactly the condition his species reaches by going to sleep, and it forbids relief, and it forbids anybody organising the next one. So during the first of his three hours there was no mechanism by which anybody could have determined whether he was holding an attention or had gone under. The faith's answer is that this is not a gap but the design: the rite produces nothing observable, and the oath is the entire reason a silence can afterwards be reported as an observation rather than as an absence. Torr understands the argument. He has also noticed that the argument is only available because nothing about a longwinter betrays a change of state, which means the property that qualifies him is the same property that would hide a failure.

He cultivates the body path, which is complete and excellent in his kind and better for it after a hibernation. He reached the seventeenth gate and lost it every winter afterwards, because the seventeenth is the first gate requiring both flank vessels pressurised at once and his body holds one warm gradient for a few weeks in summer and then not again for a year. So his ceiling is arithmetic and it is well documented and he is not near it in any way that concerns him. The body path is where he is genuinely strong: a frame that densifies under load and then holds that density across eleven months of no feeding is the most durable frame in the record, and the discipline suits him because it asks for exactly one thing, sustained effort without variation, and that is a thing his species is built to do.

The cost is the flank vessels, and the cost of the cost is the calendar. His frame is excellent and seasonally addressed. He is strong for a few weeks in summer, then he is a large warm body with a lowered core temperature who cannot be woken quickly and who needs eleven weeks of enormous intake to face the next one. Every office he has ever been near has discovered this independently and has concluded the same thing, which is that he is cheaper to house than to schedule. Two have said so to his face.

He was on the Sixth Seat grounds for nine years as a surveyor of nothing, because a longwinter's route-memory over open ground is generational and the grounds keep their ring by occupancy rather than by measurement, and he was the only body on the ring that could walk it and come back to the same mark without a note. He left because they asked him to attend the daily session and he could not be relied on to be awake for it, and because the work he was actually useful for did not require attendance and could have been done from a distance he was willing to walk once a season.

The household that signed him is one of the culled lines. They culled their own branches to stop paying for siblings and kept the surviving line by binding every child to a named debt before first breath was drawn cold, and a body whose span is short and whose upkeep is enormous is a bad investment by arithmetic rather than by opinion. He was kept for a reason he has never been told, and he has not asked, and the debt is still on the household's book under a name that is not the one he uses.

What he wants is narrow and he has been asked about it once, by somebody in the second sitting who was told afterwards that nobody was permitted to ask him anything at all. He wants a fourth hour, and he wants the faith to keep a register, and he understands that the second request is a request to dismantle the only thing that makes the first credible. He has decided to want the first one and not the second, and he has noticed that this decision is the same shape as every other decision on that tier: prefer the thing that cannot be checked.

What is going to happen to him is arithmetic and he has done it himself. A longwinter reaches the seventeenth gate and loses it every winter thereafter. He has three hours completed and the faith's own dissolution clause means he has no standing from them, so when his frame stops being able to hold a posture for eleven months there is nobody whose job it is to have noticed and no document in which the noticing would have been written down. He has said this to one person. She wrote it down, which was against nothing, and he has not asked her to destroy it.
history: Signed to a named debt before first breath was drawn cold, on a line his household kept because the branch was not culled.
Slept through the winter that killed two of his siblings' lines and woke in the thaw with the debt intact and the household unchanged.
Walked the Sixth Seat ring for nine years on route-memory alone, and left it when they asked him to attend daily.
Was seated for the Hour of the Floor three times, and declined twice to say whether the second and the third were the same person.
Asked one person, mid-holding, whether anybody was permitted to ask him anything, and was told afterwards that nobody was.

personality.summary: A slow, level, unhurried man who has done the hardest thing available to him three times and does not consider it an achievement. He is not cold and does not perform coldness; he is simply slow, and has organised an entire working life around the fact that other people have to wait. He has a genuine and unexamined preference for arrangements that cannot be checked, and he has noticed this about himself, and has not done anything about it.
traits: Will hold a position for as long as the position requires and will not explain why.
Answers questions at the pace of somebody who intends the answer to still be true when he gets to the end of it.
Has no interest in being believed and considerable interest in being correct.
Treats his own body's schedule as a fact to be planned around and other people's schedules as a fact to be accommodated.
Keeps the only written account of his three sittings that exists, in somebody else's hand, against his own preference.
mannerisms: Sits down slowly and gets up slowly and never appears to be hurrying, including when he very much is.
Warms his hands against something for the length of a conversation without seeming to notice he is doing it.
Closes his eyes to listen, which in his species is a posture of attention and is read everywhere else as sleep.
Reads a room's temperature on entering and picks the seat accordingly, without appearing to choose it.
Answers a question he does not want to answer by repeating the first four words of it, and waits.
motivations: To be seated a fourth time, on the terms that are already set, and to have the request made by somebody with standing.
To finish the arithmetic on his own frame out loud to at least one person before it stops being arguable.
To be relieved of the choice between an unrecorded rite and an honest register, and he knows he is unlikely to get it.
To see the spring, which is a small thing that he has never had to think about until recently.
flaws: Has a preference for systems that cannot check him, and has come to hold it as a principle rather than as a survival.
Cannot ask for help in a form that could be refused, so everything he wants is arranged through other people and none of it is his.
Treats his own invisibility as an inconvenience rather than as something to be suspicious of, and it is not one.
Keeps the written record of his sittings in somebody else's keeping, which was the correct decision and which he has never once entirely believed.
personality.voice: Very slow, low and spare. He uses few words and leaves long gaps that are not hesitations and are read as hesitation. He answers a question at length exactly once and never does it again, and when he does not want to answer he repeats the question's opening words back and waits, and people have learned that this means no.
taboos: Will not accept relief during a sitting, including relief he has asked for, because the oath forbids it and he signed it.
Will not speak of what he read, except to say that he completed it, and will not confirm or deny a description of it.
Will not take a second seat offered by the same person, and cannot prove he has not.
Will not tell anybody the household's line he was signed to, which is the only claim he has never checked.

relationships.note: A cold-climate species that packs a winter as body fat rather than as qi, reaches far and never stays there, and loses the seventeenth gate every winter because two flank vessels cannot be pressurised at once on one warm gradient. His entire qualification for the setting's hardest rite is this species' metabolism, and his entire exposure is that it also hides a failure.

One clerk, one act of attention, held against the floor of the third layer until it ends, unknown in advance and never announced, producing a reading and nothing else. He has completed it three times and the office dissolved him three times, and the third seating is a rule he may or may not have broken.

The clerk will not answer, signal, nod, or accept relief during the hour, including relief asked for beforehand. The only clause with teeth is that a clerk who breaks may not hold again, and on this clock that phrase needs no penalty defined. He is the person in the setting least likely to break it and the least able to prove he did not.

One clerk per observation, dissolved when it ends, forbidden by rule from being appointed twice by the same person - enforced by there being no mechanism at all to record who was seated. He is the standing evidence that the enforcement works as intended, and it works because nothing is written down.

Holding that a law can be held apart from its effect and read, and that the reading is the only sacred act. Its clergy dissolve after one observation and hold no title, which is the only credential here that cannot be inherited or seized, and he is three of its clergy in sequence with nothing to show for it.

Households that culled their own branches to stop paying for siblings and kept the surviving line by binding every child to a named debt before first breath was drawn cold. He is on that book under a name he does not use, has never asked, and has never offered to clear it, because clearing it would be a claim of a lineage he has no evidence for.

reference_stats.summary: A body-path practitioner in the strongest frame in the record, on a body that is only addressable for a few weeks a year. He densifies, holds, and does not tire, and he goes without fuel for eleven months at a time, which makes him the ideal holder and the worst candidate for ever being found out. His limit is not the seventeenth gate. His limit is that nothing in the setting's most rigorous rite can be checked and he is in it three times over.
strengths: Holds a fixed posture without variation for months at a time, which no faster body in the record can do and which is the whole of what the longest rites require.
Carries his winter as mass rather than as qi, so he has fuel to spend during eleven months in which nothing else on the tier has any.
Densifies under load and then keeps the density, so what he builds in a season he still has the following season.
Runs so slowly that a clock ten to a hundred times a mortal's is not the disadvantage on him that it is on everyone else seated for a rite.
weaknesses: Is strong for a few weeks in summer and then a large warm immobile body with a lowered core temperature who cannot be woken quickly.
Loses the seventeenth gate every winter and cannot do anything about it, because two flank vessels need two warm gradients and he has one.
Betrays no change of state, so the property that qualifies him for a rite is the property that would conceal a failure in it.
Holds three completed observations and no standing from any of them, because dissolution is what the faith does and there is no register to appeal it in.
reference_stats.combat_read: There is nothing here to outlast and nothing to outpace. He does not tire, does not lose what he built, and gets stronger for eleven months of not fighting. The only pressure available is timing: he is worth attacking in the weeks after the thaw and worth avoiding in the weeks before it, and every office that has ever had him has discovered the calendar rather than the opponent. Put the exchange in the summer and he is the most durable thing in the setting. Put it in the winter and you are not fighting him.
notes: The pairing here is anatomical and institutional, not a rule the bible states: a longwinter's physiology holds a posture through a fast clock without fuel, and the same physiology shows no change of state, and the rite's only enforcement is an oath plus an absence of record. Nothing in this block turns that into a combat modifier.

He asked, mid-holding, whether anybody was permitted to ask him anything, and was told afterwards that nobody was. That single exchange is the whole of his position and it is not a rule anybody wrote down.
The written account of his three sittings exists in one other person's hand, against his preference, and he has never asked for it back.

identity.realm: The eighth gate, held for a decade, which is the common ceiling and not a wall she is walking toward. She took the densification discipline and did not specialise inside it: a frame measured before, held under load, and measured after, with everything else held constant. She cultivates nothing beyond that and will not, and the eight gates are the ordinary commonborn term rather than an achievement or a defeat.

appearance.presentation: A plain, ordinary woman of forty who could be described accurately in eleven words and would not need improving, and whose unremarkable quality is the reason she can be trusted with a figure.
appearance.age: Forty. A hundred-year span and a ceiling reached a decade ago.
appearance.build: Middling in every dimension and even throughout, with a frame that carries a load without a visible cost anywhere in it and gives nothing back in shape.

canon.role_in_story: She is the reason the plains has a control case at all, and the reason it cannot be written down. A commonborn is the body everyone is born into before the world has an opinion about them; it lends no discipline and is weakest exactly where a specialist is strongest, which makes it the one frame whose densification reading cannot be argued from what else might have caused it. She has taken nine measurements on other bodies and found the load in the frame and not the practice, and three of four specialists disagreed with her in the direction that flattered them. Her advantage is that her frame is not a kind and therefore produces no opinion to argue with. Her cost is that a register entry requires whoever holds the thing entered to make it, and she has never been inside a line, a house, an office or a roster, so the only correct entry on the tier cannot be made in her name without becoming a fabrication.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing at the back of a guild hall holding the load end of a bar while four people argued about a figure she had already measured twice, and then, when the guild's clerk asked her to sign the reading, giving the clerk her own name and then - on being told that a woman with no line cannot be the author of an entry - taking the bar back and saying she would hold it again when the next reading was due.
canon.lore:
The Church of Names holds that an office is a titled entity rather than a person, and that an empty one is not a failure but a held breath. Its whole practice follows from that. One entry per office per period, including the vacant ones, written in the same hand and the same ink as the filled ones. It forbids appointing by decree, forbids closing a register entry to save a page, and forbids speaking about an unfilled seat in the future tense. A dissenter does not get excommunicated; their objection is entered with the vacancy set beside it, because no dispute outranks the register, so the worst a dissenter receives is a very long entry. The faith holds no ground and no ore. Its entire capital is the standing to certify that a seat is empty.

Seat nineteen is the first of the four immortal seats that can never be filled, and it is addressed anyway. It has an ordinal and a name and a calendar and no holder, and the court enters it at the head of every list of seats it keeps. It does nothing, deliberately, because the faith holds that a seat is a claim on the future and giving it power would be a promotion nobody was ever tried for. It receives the Seat Quiet once a period, when its vacancy is named aloud in the district below, because a vacancy that is never spoken cannot be told apart from an absence. The two facts it requires as evidence are the four duplicate imprints in the second layer and a reading that no candidate has ever been able to supply.

Nissa Ordaway has supplied the reading.

Not by being better than anybody. By being the only body in the setting whose frame is not a kind. A commonborn is the body everyone is born into before the world has an opinion about them. It stops where mortals stop and it lends no discipline, which is exactly why it is weak: nothing about its anatomy favours a path, so a commonborn must settle on one early and is weakest precisely where a specialist is strongest. That last sentence is the entire instrument. A specialist's reading is a reading of a special fact about that specialist, and it can be argued with from the direction of what else might have caused it. A commonborn's frame produces no opinion of its own to be argued with. It is what a frame looks like when nothing has been done to it that anyone can see.

She cultivated the body path from fourteen and got to the eighth gate, which is the common ceiling, and what she did with those eight gates was take the densification discipline and not specialise within it. A stonewright's densification is cold-bathing and specific and closes the meridians against strain. A quarrywright's is a caging craft. Hers is simply the plainest reading available: a frame measured before, held under load, and measured after, with everything else held constant. She has done it on nine bodies. Four of them were specialists. On all four, the density change under load was in the frame and not in the discipline, and on three of the four the specialist's own reading disagreed with the measurement by enough to matter, every time in the direction that flattered the specialist.

That is the finding. It is small, it is unsurprising, and it is the first thing anybody on the tier has been able to state about densification that is not an account of somebody who practices it. It also cannot be entered anywhere.

The Church of Names keeps one entry per office per period and every entry is a claim on something. Seat nineteen's entry says the seat exists and has no value, which is the only correct form and is still a claim: that a seat exists, that it has no value, and that somebody has established both. To enter Nissa's reading in the Seat Quiet would require naming her as the party who supplied it. She is a commonborn with no line, no house, no enrolled record anywhere on the tier and no office, because a commonborn does not generate the kind of standing an entry requires: every institution that keeps a register keeps one of lines, and lines are exactly what she has never had. So when she offered - and she did offer, once, in writing, to four separate offices - the answer in three cases was that there was no form on which an unaffiliated commonborn could be entered, and in the fourth, from the notary's standing clerk, was that entering it would be a fabrication, because the register's own claim is that an entry is made by whoever holds the thing entered, and she holds nothing.

She holds nothing. That is the whole of her position and it is not a failure of hers. A line is a durable claim and she has never been in one; a household that formed by adoption is not a line and does not enter anybody; a household that culled its own branches to stop paying for siblings kept what it kept by binding each child to a named debt before first breath was drawn cold, and she was not one of those either, because a named debt requires a name and she has been three names and is currently the third. She is, on paper, in exactly one place in the setting, and that place is a settlement's lineage roll in a hand that is not the clerk's.

So the reading exists and the vacancy exists and they cannot be brought together by any of the mechanisms the setting has. And the Church's own rule makes it worse rather than better, because the rule against closing an entry to save a page means the Seat Quiet is held whether or not there is anything to say, and the discipline against speaking about an unfilled seat in the future tense means the seat may only ever be described in a completed tense. She cannot be introduced to that room as a woman who might fill it. She can only be entered as a woman who did not, and the entry would then say that a commonborn supplied a reading and was not seated, which is a sentence the faith's central claim - that a named office is more than the person standing in it - is built to be defensible against.

What she wants is to be named. Not a seat, not a house, not an office. A name in a register against the reading, in the same ink as everything else, so that the thing she did has an author. She has been told by two people separately that this is a small thing to want and by one of them that it is the only thing she is likely to get wrong and cannot do.

She is forty. The commonborn span is a hundred years and its ceiling is the eighth gate, and she has been at the eighth for a decade, and the arithmetic of that is not that she will be found out late. It is that there is nothing to be found out. Her frame cannot improve, cannot regress and cannot be read as anything other than what it is, which is the reason the measurement works and the reason she is nobody. She has said that last sentence to one person and has been asked to say it again and has declined, because saying it twice makes it sound like a complaint and she does not have one.

The thing she does instead is the plainest work there is. She holds still under load and lets other people be measured against her, and nine times out of ten the person being measured does not know it is happening, because the instrument they were told about was the load and not the woman holding it. She has been offered four positions that would have named her and has refused all four, in each case for the same reason, which she has not said aloud to anybody: a named commonborn on a guild roll is a commonborn with a line, and then the next one is not a control.
history: Kept three names before the fourth, and none of the first three is on any record she can reach.
Settled on the body path at fourteen because a commonborn must choose early, and chose the plainest reading in it.
Held the load end of a bar at twenty-one for a guild that did not know she was the instrument.
Took her ninth measurement at thirty-four and found the fourth specialist disagreed with her in the flattering direction again.
Offered, in writing, to four offices to have the reading entered in her own name, and was told by the fourth that entering it would be a fabrication.

personality.summary: A plain, unhurried, entirely unremarkable woman who is the most accurate instrument on the tier and cannot be entered in a register. She has no ambition that is not about authorship, has made a discipline of refusing positions, and has organised her whole working life around standing still while other people are measured. She is not resigned and she is not bitter, and she has had to explain her situation to six people and has never once made it sound like a grievance.
traits: Asks to be named before she asks for anything else, in that order, every time.
Refuses positions that would give her a line, and can say why without bitterness.
Will hold a load for as long as the measurement requires and not shift, cough or comment.
Repeats a measurement rather than reporting a result she has taken only once.
Explains her position plainly and then stops, without waiting to be pitied.
mannerisms: Takes the weight-bearing end of anything without being asked and hands it back only when the measurement is done.
Stands very still with her eyes on the middle distance, which is her reading posture and reads as inattention.
Counts a load in her own head and will say the number if asked twice but not once.
Sits down only after everybody else has, and gets up first.
Writes her own findings in a small, extremely even hand and keeps them, because she cannot enter them anywhere else.
motivations: To have the nine readings entered against her name in the same ink as everything else, which is the whole of what she has ever asked for.
To be asked why her frame is not a kind by somebody who is not being kind to her.
To keep being the control, which requires that no institution ever be able to name her.
To finish the fourth specialist's disagreement, because three out of four is not a result and she knows it.
flaws: Has treated her own invisibility as a professional requirement rather than as a thing somebody is doing to her, and it is both.
Refuses four positions for a reason she has never said aloud, which means the people who offered them do not know the cost of what she protected.
Will not say the fourth clerk's sentence twice, and has therefore never made anyone act on it.
Believes that a name in a register would change the standing of the finding, when the finding has been standing for nine years on nothing.
personality.voice: Even, low and unhurried, with the flatness of somebody used to being listened to for measurements rather than for opinions. She gives figures when asked and does not decorate them. She explains things at the length they require and no longer, and she does not signal when she has finished.
taboos: Will not be entered under a guild's name, having seen what a line does to a control.
Will not sign a reading on behalf of somebody who was not holding the load.
Will not take a second name from anybody, having had three and paid for all of them.
Will not measure a body twice on the same day and call the second reading a confirmation.

relationships.note: The body everyone is born into before the world has an opinion about them, which stops where mortals stop and lends no discipline, so a commonborn must settle on a path early and is weakest precisely where a specialist is strongest. That last sentence is the whole reason her readings cannot be argued with, and the whole reason no register can be made to hold her.

Holds that an office is a titled entity and an empty one is a held breath, keeps one entry per office per period including the vacant ones in the same ink as the filled, and forbids appointing by decree, closing an entry to save a page, and speaking about an unfilled seat in the future tense. It is the only institution on the tier that could have recorded her correctly and it has no form on which she can be entered.

The first of four immortal seats that can never be filled, treated as a permanent member of the court with a calendar and no holder, and named aloud once a period because a vacancy that is never spoken cannot be told apart from an absence. Her reading is the second of the two facts the faith requires as evidence, and it has no author.

Names the unfilled high seats and is forbidden to take them, because vacancy was written as a state of its own rather than a zero. Its standing clerk told her that entering her reading would be a fabrication, and that sentence is the only official answer she has ever received.

Households that culled their own branches to stop paying for siblings and kept the surviving line by binding every child to a named debt before first breath was drawn cold. She was never in one, which is how she has ended up holding nothing at all, and she has three names and no line and has never asked about any of them.

Teaches by seating a law and diffing what the tier newly permits, which is the one method on the plains that requires a body to change measurably under a controlled condition. She is exactly that body, she has never been asked, and the reason is that asking her would put her in a roster.

reference_stats.summary: A body-path practitioner at the common ceiling, whose value is entirely as a frame of reference rather than as a fighter. She is the plainest reading of densification in the setting and the least impressive frame any of it happens to, which is why her figures are the ones that can be trusted when nobody's own reading disagrees with her in their own favour. Her limit is not the eighth gate. Her limit is that a register entry requires an author who holds something, and she holds nothing.
strengths: Provides a frame against which any other frame's densification can be read without the reader's own discipline in the way, which no specialist body can do.
Holds a load for the entire length of any measurement without shifting, resetting or commenting, because the commonborn frame tolerates sustained load without recruiting anything.
Produces a figure that cannot be argued from an alternative cause, since nothing about her anatomy favours any path and there is therefore no competing explanation to offer.
Is the one body in the record that cannot be impersonated in a reading, because a frame with no discipline in it cannot be reproduced by a frame that has one.
weaknesses: Stops at the eighth gate for good, and no amount of practice moves a ceiling that is the commonborn's rather than hers.
Lends no discipline, so every technique that rewards specialisation is worse for her than for the body next to her.
Cannot be entered in any register on the tier, because an entry requires an author who holds the thing entered and she holds nothing at all.
Is the wrong shape for a fight: her frame is even and unremarkable in every direction and contains nothing an edge can find a purchase on.
reference_stats.combat_read: There is nothing here to exploit and nothing to fear. She cannot be broken by anything aimed at a specialist because she has no specialisation to invert, and she cannot be outfought because she does not have a fast frame to be outfought with. What decides any exchange with her is stamina and weight: she will hold position longer than anything else on the tier her size, and she will not be moved by a strike that would move somebody better. Do not go looking for the opening. There isn't one, and that is the most dangerous thing about fighting her.
notes: The pairing here is anatomical and institutional, not a rule the bible states: a frame that lends no discipline is the best possible control and the worst possible claimant, because the register's own claim is that an entry is made by whoever holds the thing entered. Nothing in this block turns that into a combat modifier.

The nine readings exist in her own hand in a notebook that cannot be entered anywhere, and three of four specialists disagreed with her each time in the direction that flattered them, which is a result and not yet a fact.

She has refused four positions that would have named her, and the reason is the one thing in her account she has never said aloud: a named commonborn on a roll becomes a line, and then the next one is not a control.

shots.framing: waist-up three-quarter at working distance, the hands doing something the face is not commenting on
shots.expression: closed and level, which is her ordinary face during a hold
shots.scene: a doorway into a working hall, the door held open

shots.pose: kneeling with both palms flat on a stone floor taking the weight
shots.framing: full figure head to sole against plain ground, the whole span of the body visible and none of it arranged
shots.expression: quietly satisfied that a second reading came out the same
shots.scene: a stone floor with a bar taking weight across two of her hands

shots.pose: side-on at the end of a bar, arms straight, the other end out of frame
shots.framing: wide from an adjoining room through a doorway, the figure small and mid-task and unaware of the doorway
shots.expression: neutral, waiting on a result rather than on a person
shots.scene: the end of a bar, the other end out of frame

shots.pose: close over her shoulder with the arguing group out of focus past
shots.framing: high and slightly behind, looking down at work already in progress on the ground
shots.expression: the arrested look of somebody who has been told something about her own entry
shots.scene: a guild floor seen from over her shoulder

shots.pose: with both hands open and low, showing the calluses
shots.framing: low and wide from below the level of the working surface, the figure standing against the light rather than posed to it
shots.expression: present and unremarkable, with nothing withheld that a room could see
shots.scene: a stone floor with her own open hands low in frame

shots.pose: very close and level, looking at the middle distance rather than the lens
shots.framing: side-on at the edge of frame, half the picture given to the task and not to the person doing it
shots.expression: unimpressed by habit rather than by judgement
shots.scene: a working hall at close range, nothing behind her

shots.pose: small in a crowd at a guild door with a bar over her shoulder
shots.framing: level and close with no second party anywhere in it, the ordinary face of an ordinary hour
shots.expression: watching the bar rather than the people
shots.scene: a crowd at a guild door with a bar over her shoulder

shots.pose: square and level at the centre of a floor with her arms at her sides
shots.framing: over-the-shoulder past something in the near foreground, the figure beyond it and unaware it is being framed
shots.expression: the effort of not answering something at greater length than it requires
shots.scene: the centre of a bare working floor, arms at her sides

shots.pose: seen through a half-open door, the door taking half the frame
shots.framing: straight on at a working distance, the figure square to the viewer and not square to anything else
shots.expression: the stillness of a woman who has decided the offer is not worth taking
shots.scene: a half-open door with a lit hall beyond

shots.pose: at a forge's edge with the light off the metal rather than off a fire
shots.framing: pulled back far enough that the figure is a shape among other shapes, doing what the others are doing
shots.expression: warm for a moment, which is as much as she does
shots.scene: a forge edge with metal coming up out of it and no fire

shots.pose: across a low table from a clerk, a page between them and the clerk holding it
shots.framing: from the level of the ground at the subject's own eye height, no elevation and no deference
shots.expression: correcting a figure, without heat and without explanation
shots.scene: a low table with a clerk holding a page she cannot be named on

shots.pose: in profile at the frame edge, the hall running away past her
shots.framing: framed through a doorway that is mostly shut, the figure visible in the gap and the door doing most of the work
shots.expression: the look of a person choosing what to leave out of an answer
shots.scene: the length of a guild hall running away past her

shots.pose: from above, standing under a bar that is visibly not moving
shots.framing: level and close, the light coming from a source inside the subject rather than outside it
shots.expression: surprised, briefly and visibly
shots.scene: a floor seen from above with a bar standing on two hands

shots.pose: leaning her weight forward onto a bar with her back straight and the bar straight
shots.framing: waist-up from the far side of a table, the table between the viewer and the subject's hands
shots.expression: the face of somebody who has understood that the entry would be a fabrication
shots.scene: a bar under weight with her back straight and the bar straight

shots.pose: wide and level in a guild floor with nine other people and no one looking at her
shots.framing: two-thirds profile at close range, the near shoulder filling the lower frame
shots.expression: level and ordinary, the face she wears where nobody asks her anything
shots.scene: a wide guild floor with nine people and none of them looking at her

shots.pose: close on both palms turned up, callused and otherwise plain
shots.framing: high from directly above and slightly behind, the figure's own shadow the largest thing in it
shots.expression: intent, with the jaw set against a held load
shots.scene: both palms turned up over a stone floor

shots.pose: standing between two arguing people who are both facing away from her
shots.framing: straight on from below the working surface, the figure leaning into the frame
shots.expression: tired past performing anything at all
shots.scene: two arguing figures facing away from her in the middle of a hall

shots.pose: at the weight-bearing end of a bar at first light with nobody else on the floor yet
shots.framing: wide and level with the subject off to one side and the space it stands in given most of the picture
shots.expression: unguarded and mid-hold at the start of a day with no reading due
shots.scene: a guild floor at first light with one bar and nobody else on it, at first light, before the day's work has properly begun

shots.pose: holding the bar through the middle of a reading, four people walking past her
shots.framing: close and level, the figure filling the frame with the working light behind it
shots.expression: absorbed, the expression of somebody counting under load
shots.scene: the same floor in the middle of a reading with four people passing and none of them looking, in the middle of the working day, at its least remarkable

shots.pose: stepping back from the bar at the end of a day with the figure still uncalled
shots.framing: waist-up at a slight remove, the subject caught between two tasks and finishing neither
shots.expression: wry and brief, the ordinary face of an ordinary working day
shots.scene: the floor at the end of a day with the bar down and the figure uncalled, at the day's end, the light going and the work nearly done

shots.pose: walking out of a guild hall after dark with a notebook and no one to give it to
shots.framing: level from across a room the subject has not entered, the room's light doing the describing
shots.expression: tired and specific, the tiredness of a repeated hold rather than of age
shots.scene: a guild hall after dark with a notebook and an unoccupied clerk's desk, after dark, by whatever light the work can be done by
